title: Tavelo Arow - Final Thoughts 5000km - Highly Recommend

takeaways.text: At 183 cm he rides the 540 size, which he equates to a long 56, with a 130 mm stem and 36 cm Tavelo AVRO integrated bar, which he praises for ergonomics and stiffness.
With 1,300 g wheels, a Dura-Ace cassette and lighter carbon cranks, his fully loaded bike weighs exactly 7 kg, which he estimates as about 6.7 kg weighed the industry-standard way.
After a year and 5,000 km he reports no creaks, rattles, failures, seatpost slips, headset problems or undersized bottom bracket, and rates the finish and paint on par with Specialized.

A pure race bike with a stiff, communicative front end, a little more comfortable than a Propel; his Tarmac SL8 climbed better and handled crosswinds better but felt softer at the bottom bracket than the Arow.
The geometry is aggressive, and the slack 73° seat angle means smaller or more upright riders may need to push the saddle forward.
He considers the roughly US$2,000 frameset price not cheap for a Chinese frame and expects poor resale value, but still highly recommends it for riders who keep a bike a long time.
He says the frame fits 34 mm tires measured at the rim. This is his field report, above the 32 mm manufacturer maximum.

disclosure: Owner long-term review with a referral to a US dealer (Sky Sports). The 2025 video covers the original Arow frameset and does not say whether it matches the current Race or SL version.
summary: Final thoughts after almost a year and 5,000 km on a Tavelo Arow frameset built for criterium racing.
